stories.title: FIFA scraps plans for private investment into World Cup
stories.summary: FIFA "will not proceed" with plans to sell stakes in a company which would run the commercial and operational aspects of its competitions, a statement from president Gianni Infantino said. The plan, which would include the men's and women’s World Cups, has been rejected by three continental confederations with UEFA insisting its nations would boycott FIFA events. In a statement released in the early hours of Saturday morning, Infantino said: "The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed. "And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

stories.title: EU accuses Temu of hindering raid in Ireland
stories.summary: The EU has accused Temu of failing to hand over information during an inspection in Dublin as part of a probe into the Chinese-owned online retailer. The EU's powerful antitrust sheriff said it carried out surprise raids between 2 and 5 December 2025, seeking evidence in an investigation looking at whether Temu received "potentially distortive foreign subsidies". The European Commission said it "preliminarily finds that Temu has infringed its duty to actively cooperate on multiple aspects related to the conduct of the inspection" at a premises of its subsidiary, WhaleCo, in Dublin. Temu rejected the EU's findings. Temu "cooperated fully and complied with all the requests the commission made during the inspection", the company said, adding it will analyse the commission's claim.

stories.summary: Bank of Ireland has reported a 33% jump in pre-tax profits for the six months to the end of June and said it was upgrading its guidance for the full year. Lending during the six month period rose by 4% to €84 billion. stories.title: At least 34 killed in coal mine blast in Pakistan
stories.summary: A blast at a coal mine killed at least 34 workers in southern Pakistan, the provincial disaster agency said, adding rescuers were searching for more missing miners. The explosion, caused by methane gas, tore through the mine near the capital of the resource-rich province of Balochistan yesterday, sparking a rescue operation that ran into the night. "According to information received from the deployed teams, 34 bodies have been recovered," southern Balochistan's provincial disaster management authority said in a statement in the early hours of this morning. "The joint rescue operation is still underway to locate and recover the remaining trapped miners," it added, without specifying how many were in the mine when the explosion took place.

stories.title: Shots galore, faith and pressing - Who adopts Mayo plan?
stories.summary: Andy Moran stepped down as Leitrim manager two years ago this month, and he left with some of his players not totally convinced by his philosophy towards the game. It was a three-year spell that mixed the good with the bad. Promotion from Division 3 in his final season was a massive boon, but there were lowlights too, particularly in the Connacht championship – a 23-point hammering at the hands of Galway, just 0-06 at home to Sligo and, most famously of all, the first ever manager to lose a provincial game to New York. After that 2024 season came to an end, it's believed that a few Leitrim players were feeling disillusioned, even if such thoughts were never uttered in front of the microphone of a reporter. Fast-forward two years and it’s inevitable that in the coming weeks some politician will, with genuine sincerity, call for a statue of Andy Moran to be built.

stories.title: Tyrrell: Galway have yet to show 'mettle' in decider
stories.summary: Former Dublin footballer Hannah Tyrrell believes Kerry have the experience and form to win another All-Ireland title and reckons that Galway have yet to show their "mettle" in a decider. Sunday's senior All-Ireland football decider is a repeat of the 2024 final, where Kerry bridged a 31-year gap to their last title, cantering home by 12 points. Captain Síofra O'Shea racked up 1-08 as Kerry comprehensively dispatched the reigning champions Dublin in the Thurles semi-final, winning 2-16 to 1-09 in the finish and they enter the finale as clear favourites. The westerners, who claimed another Connacht title earlier this year, easily accounted for Armagh in the other semi.

Aer Lingus said today that its costs increased by 8% in the first half of the year and passenger revenue decreased by 3%.

stories.title: Inside the French town hit hardest by wildfires

Le Porge is considered the epicentre of the devastating wildfires that tore through the region over the past week and, in places, continue to smoulder. When the alarm was raised on Friday, the town was swiftly evacuated. But when the residents returned, it was to scenes of ruin. 183 homes had been consumed by the fire - many are now roofless, hollow shells.

stories.summary: FIFA is seeking an independent agency to assess the expansion of the men's World Cup to 64 teams. FIFA’s president Gianni Infantino is under increasing pressure amid mounting opposition to plans to seek private investment in a company which would run the World Cup, with three confederations having rejected it and his senior adviser having quit over it. One of the key concerns around the plan was the potential for private investors to seek ever bigger, ever more frequent tournaments to maximise returns. Now the Press Association has seen documents in which FIFA expresses its wish to appoint an independent agency to assess an expansion to 64 teams from the current 48, starting with the next finals in 2030.

Cardiff, owned by the Welsh Rugby Union, and Dragons, an independently backed business, are set to be given licences, leaving Swansea-based Ospreys and Llanelli-based Scarlets to compete for the remaining spot. Ospreys have won the URC, in its previous guise, four times, most recently in 2012.

stories.title: 100 Buildings: A Modernist surprise on the streets of Dungarvan
stories.summary: The Dungarvan Further Education and Training Centre is an unexpected Modern Movement gem in the suburbs of Dungarvan, County Waterford, on a corner site bounded by Wolfe Tone Road and O'Connell Street. If walking by, do look closer at the entrance for a sign of its past. In 1899, technical schools were set up in Ireland to provide more practical vocational training. The 1930 Vocational Education Act gave local councils the funds to develop technical education further with the building of bespoke vocational schools. Many charged nominal fees, which were small compared to the cost of going to secondary school. Free secondary school education was not available until 1967. In 1933, the Waterford County Surveyor, John Kingston Bowen (1888–1944), was tasked with designing a vocational school for Dungarvan. Scoil na gCeárd (translates to vocational school). The school building was officially opened on the 5th of April 1939, with Thomas Derrig (1897–1956), Minister for Education, in attendance. John was brother to Richard Bowen, County Surveyor for Kilkenny, who designed the Padmore and Barnes Boot Factory. The Waterford County VEC amalgamated with Wexford in 2011 and today the building is run by Dungarvan Further Education and Training Centre, which still provides training for adults across Waterford and Wexford. The school is a well-proportioned five-bay, two-storey, flat-roofed building in the International Style, with a single-bay, two-storey advanced entrance bay and a two-storey return. The entrance is sheltered by a concrete canopy, over which there is a rendered panel with raised lettering spelling out 'Scoil na gCeárd' in beautiful Gaelic letterform. The painted rendered walls give the building a clean appearance, and the low rendered boundary wall, piers, and pedestrian gate (blocked) still remain. All the windows were unfortunately replaced by uPVC casement windows in the early nineties. It is set back from the road, and its geometric form and massing are softened by mature trees.

stories.summary: Singer Boy George has pulled out of a West End production of the musical Jesus Christ Superstar after facing a backlash for releasing a pro-Israel song, We Will Dance Again. The 65-year-old musician "will no longer be appearing in Jesus Christ Superstar at the London Palladium", his manager Paul Kemsley said on social media. The singer, whose real name is George Alan O'Dowd, rose to fame in the 1980s as the flamboyant frontman of the pop band Culture Club. This week, he released a song supporting Israel and its war in Gaza, with lyrics including "you say genocide, I say war" and "when you're attacked, that's what the army's for".

stories.title: What is the luteal phase, and why are women tracking it?
stories.summary: Women's reproductive health has undergone something of a PR transformation in recent years, with more discourse emerging around working with your hormones, tapping into the power of the period and what it all signifies about a woman's overall health. Periods, and understanding your period, have become a hot topic of conversation, but none more so than one specific part of it: the luteal phase. Google searches for the term 'luteal phase' have increased 300% in recent years, and a cursory glance at social media posts on the topic will see it blamed for everything from brain fog and sugar cravings to falling out of love with your partner. The luteal phase, Wallace says, is the second half of the menstrual cycle, spanning from ovulation (when an egg is released) to the next period.

stories.title: France, Italy bolster border controls due to Ceuta crisis
stories.summary: France and Italy have bolstered border controls after around 60,000 people crossed into the Spanish territory of Ceuta in North Africa, sparking one of the largest migrant crises for the European Union in recent years. The migrants entered Ceuta from Morocco, the regional president Juan Jesus Vivas told reporters, but by yesterday evening officials said more than 48,000 had returned. To cross into Ceuta, many swam around a small border barrier that juts out into the Mediterranean. At least 34 people died in the attempt. A high-level crisis meeting of senior EU officials is set to take place today in response to the crisis.

stories.title: Pico sees red in Shamrock Rovers stalemate at Drogheda
stories.summary: Pico Lopes can do no wrong, until he can. Exactly four weeks to the day that the Crumlin-born Cape Verde star went toe-to-toe with Lionel Messi and Argentina in the World Cup round of 32 clash in Miami, the Shamrock Rovers captain was shown his marching orders in injury time at Drogheda United. The home fans enjoyed that one. The man watched by hundreds of millions of fans around the world just a few weeks ago, now sent off in front of 2,289 in Drogheda. He can have few complaints about it, his challenge on Shane Farrell was late and high. It didn't affect the outcome of the game, this one had scoreless draw written all over it at half-time as those in attendance stewed over a game severely lacking in quality. There was a time in the not so distant past that Rovers went five SSE Airtricity Men's Premier Division games without a victory against Drogheda, the Louth men laying credible claim to the title of the Hoops’ bogey team.
